sample_type.evidence_source: [/page/2/Text/14] In both waves, a paper-and-pencil survey was distributed during school hours after acquiring active consent from the schools and teachers, and passive consent from respondents' parents (i.e., parents were informed and could reply if they refused their child to participate). Respondents were assured that their answers would be analyzed only by the principal investigators, and not shown to their teachers or parents. In order to match responses from the two waves, respondents were required to fill in either their name, or their personal student number.
